Description: What a message is, before any reader reads it: the examples the router of Lambek compares a message with. Written by hand, taken from the small talk of the language files, the examples of the packs, and the calibration splits of the benches; never from a test split.

Acts.Talk: small talk: greetings, thanks, questions about Lambek
Acts.Feeling: the user says how they feel
Acts.Order: an order Lambek can carry out: files, code, and what follows one ("et dans C:\Data ?")
Acts.Elsewhere: an order for something Lambek has no hold on: messages, calls, shopping, the house
Acts.Tell: something told to remember: a fact, a rule, a condition, a default
Acts.Ask: a question about what was told, or that follows from it
Acts.World: a question about the world, that nothing told answers: general knowledge, the time, the weather
Acts.Why: why something is, or how Lambek knows it
Acts.Problem: a word problem: numbers told, then a question
Acts.Open: a request with no single answer: a story, a poem, advice, an opinion, the future

Router.Description: Set on the calibration split of bench/acts.json: the nearest examples that vote, the passes of the learnt vectors, the margin under which the router abstains, and the weight of each kind of feature
